deliverables, with Show SDR Version to preview the last.
→ [HDR and colour management](docs/guide/hdr-and-color.md)

**Motion graphics.** Graphic clips drawn every frame by a small JavaScript
module: 23 built-ins: charts, a gauge and timers, screencast keys and window
frames, title, quote and logo cards, and social pop-ups, properties as
inspector controls, your own modules too.
→ [Motion graphics](docs/guide/graphics.md)

**Screen recording.** A display or a window, with system audio, microphone and
click rings, at 30 or 60 fps, into a new project or at the playhead; a camera,
604:**GR-13 — The bundled templates look and move right**
605-- **Setup:** a 1920×1080 project with a video clip on it, a 1080×1920 project and a 1080×1080 project; View ▸ Safe Areas on; View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full.
606-- **Do:** In each project, insert each of the 23 templates (Insert ▸ Graphic ▸ …), over the clip in the 1080p project, then play each from its start to its end.
607-- **Expect:** smooth entrances and outros, readable text, and nothing drawn past the Safe guide's outer (90 %, title-safe) rectangle at any moment, in every project.
608-- **Answer:** for each template that fails, its name, the project (1080p, 1080×1920 or 1080×1080) and what is wrong: a jerky move, text you cannot read, or something past the outer rectangle.
609-- **Source:** owner 2026-10-29 (spec §11 G-44); `graphic/tests/templates.rs` measures that nothing outside title-safe moves at every fifth frame and that no frame warns, not how the motion looks.
610-
611-## Mattes
612-
--
731:- **Expect:** the pick turns hue and saturation on around the skin; Show Selection shows the face white and greys and dark noise black (the chroma and near-black guards), the "Selection" tag beside the preview; the softness widens the edge smoothly with no hard ring; only the face warms, and the background and greys stay as they were; selecting a media clip turns Show Selection off and Esc leaves a pick; each strip drag and each pick undoes in one step (Hue, Saturation, Luma, Qualifier); the export is the graded picture, never the selection; the strips, knobs, squares and fields read clearly in both appearances at every width, and playback stays smooth. If the guards pick dark noise or drop real skin, the first numbers in spec §11 GR-13 are what to retune. (T4-4) Blur melts the speckle into a smooth grey edge without growing the selection onto the background, the same at Full and Half; the blur undoes in one step named Qualifier Blur and Reset sets it to 0 %; with the blur on, 4K playback stays smooth (no dropped frames you can see); if 100 % is too little or too much on real footage, the 24 px of spec §11 GR-35 is the number to retune.
732:- **Source:** grading-2's G2-4 (spec §11 GR-13) and grading-4's T4-4 (GR-35); `tools/proof/qualifier_proof.py` measures the ranges on synthetic hue, saturation and ramp cards and the blur on a synthetic noise card against a scripted Gaussian, not how a selection holds up on skin.
733-
734-**GRD-15 — A sky inside a shape**
735-- **Do:** 1. Open footage with a sky and add an adjustment clip over it with a qualifier on the blue of the sky (Pick from Canvas on it) and Light ▸ Exposure −0.5. 2. Add a track in front of the adjustment clip's, draw a rectangle shape over the top half and make that track an alpha matte. 3. Turn Show Selection on and off; move the rectangle down over something else blue. 4. Animate the qualifier's hue centre with an action from blue to cyan and play it.
736-- **Expect:** only the sky inside the rectangle darkens — blue outside it and the rest of the frame are untouched; Show Selection shows white only where the sky meets the rectangle; moving the rectangle moves the darkened area; the animated centre sweeps the short way between the two hues, never through red.
737:- **Source:** grading-2's G2-4 (spec §11 GR-13, matte × qualifier); `qualifier_proof.py`'s M1 measures the product on a card.
738-
739-**GRD-16 — iPhone HDR footage**
740-- **Do:** 1. Import an ordinary iPhone HDR clip (default Camera settings, HEVC) into a project of its own. 2. Look at it in the preview — with the playhead parked, paused, on the clip's first frame, and again just after Play from there; then play the composition through to its end — save a frame (File ▸ Save Frame…) and export a short GIF, and compare each side by side with the clip in QuickTime Player. 3. Export `prores_422` and step through the first frames where the clip starts in QuickTime Player. 4. Select the clip, open the Chroma Key section, press Pick from Canvas and click something green (or any distinct colour) in the frame; play. 5. Re-run PRC-3's HLG half (steps 1, 2 and 4) on this clip. 6. In another project, put a short Frame Job screen recording (File ▸ New Recording…) beside the iPhone HDR clip, and look at the recording there, in a project of its own, and in QuickTime Player. 7. (hdr H-2) In the first project set the Document tab's Dynamic Range to HDR (HLG) and repeat step 4's key on the same colour; export `hevc_10bit` and open it in QuickTime Player.
741-- **Expect:** the preview, the saved frame and the GIF all look like QuickTime Player's picture — not flat and grey, highlights rolling off rather than clipping, saturated colours not clipped; the preview's first frame, paused and on Play, is not washed out, and playback to the end stays smooth and never turns washed out; no washed-out flash on the clip's first exported frame; the key removes the colour that was picked, in the preview and in an export; PRC-3's expectations hold; the screen recording looks the same in all three places; the clip's timeline filmstrip and its Media-tab thumbnail look like the preview (spec §11 GR-21); (step 7) in the HLG project the clip's highlights are brighter than in the SDR one on an XDR display and nothing washes out, the key still removes the colour with no re-pick (in an HLG project a key on an HDR clip compares the colour an SDR project shows, spec §11 HD-19 (c)), a fresh pick in the HLG project keys the same colour, and the HEVC file looks the same in QuickTime Player as in the preview.
742-- **Source:** grading-3 T3-1 (spec §11 GR-15 as amended: Frame Job's own HDR→SDR at step 0, chosen per composition, and the sRGB arm), and step 7's key clean-up batch 2's phase 2 (HD-19 (c), #312); `tools/proof/hdr_proof.py` measures synthetic ramps and greens (HKh), not real footage, and its R0 read only a recording's labels.
743-
744-**GRD-17 — Apple Log footage**
745-- **Do:** 1. Import an iPhone Apple Log clip (iPhone 15 Pro or later, ProRes with Log, or Blackmagic Camera in Apple Log; or Apple Log 2 from a newer iPhone) into a project of its own. 2. Select its row in the Media tab and read the Camera Log section. 3. Set Camera Log to None, then back to the detected setting. 4. On the clip, Color: raise Brightness a little; then Look: apply Warm. 5. If you have Apple's Apple Log LUT, import it with Use LUT… and compare with the built-in conversion. 6. Note the 18 % grey patch or a face's level in the preview with the waveform open.
2286:- **G-44 — The bundled templates: one unit, title-safe at every frame,
2287-  a static card, the bundled faces, generic glyphs, an accent and an
2288-  outro, held by a test** (owner, 2026-10-29: "I want to create some more
2289-  default graphics"; seventeen added to road map 10's six).
2290-  (a) **The unit.** A template sizes everything by
2291-  `u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080`, which is the six's
2292-  `ctx.height / 1080` in landscape and keeps a portrait (1080 × 1920)
2293-  frame from drawing at 1.78 times the size.
2294-  (b) **Title-safe at every frame.** Everything a template draws, at
2295-  every frame, lies inside the 90 % title-safe rectangle
2296-  (x ∈ [0.05W, 0.95W), y ∈ [0.05H, 0.95H)), at 1920 × 1080, at
2297-  1080 × 1920 and at 1080 × 1080 (the square social canvas, which takes
2298-  the landscape layout). An entrance is a spring, a clipPath wipe or a
2299-  fade, never a move in from off-frame.
2300-  (c) **A card's background is static.** A full-frame template (one that
2301-  passes `background` to `svg`) draws the same background at frame 0 as at
2302-  every later frame; its outro fades or moves the content only.
2303-  (d) **The faces.** Montserrat 800/900 for text, IBM Plex Mono 500 for
2304-  ticking digits, and `'Source Sans 3'` 600 only for window-frame's UI
2305-  text. Bundled faces only (G-6).
2306-  (e) **Glyphs.** A keycap symbol, a bell, a heart, a play triangle or a
2307-  platform glyph is a generic vector shape drawn by the module; no brand's
2308-  artwork.
2309-  (f) **Accent and outro.** Every template has an `accent` colour prop and
2310-  an outro in about its last 15 frames, keyed to `ctx.durationInFrames`,
2311-  that leaves its last frame bare: clear for an overlay, the background
2312-  alone for a card.
2313-  (g) **The test.** `graphic/tests/templates.rs` holds every module of
2314-  `graphic/tests/graphics/` except `common::FIXTURES` (road map 10's six,
2315-  which keep their own look and pins) to (b), (c) and (f)'s bare last
2316-  frame at all three sizes, with its defaults and with every combination
2317-  of its `enum` options: every sampled frame equals frame 0 outside
2318-  title-safe, and frame 0 has one alpha value there; no warning from `svg`
2319-  or `rasterize`, no `NaN` or `Infinity` in the SVG, with defaults and with
2320-  degenerate data (one point, an all-zero series, `max ≤ min`); and
2321-  `project.yml`'s "Copy Graphic Templates" lists exactly the folder's
2322-  `*.js` files.
